reasons: The finding is correctly classified: Article XII runs only in Licensor's favour and Article XIII(a) affirmatively disclaims any Licensor liability for infringement claims, so the playbook's required Vendor IP indemnity is genuinely absent (walk-away scenario).

The inserted Licensor indemnity tracks the model language closely — third-party IP infringement/misappropriation, breach of law, unauthorised access to Licensee data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct — and adds the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure required by the preferred position.

Narrowing the Licensee indemnity to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of applicable law (and deleting the open-ended 'solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability' language) is exactly the 'Customer's indemnity stays narrow' element of the rule.
The express carve-out from Article XIII's exclusions and cap is substantively necessary, not overreach: without it the IP disclaimer and the one-half-of-fees cap would nullify the new indemnity.

High changed-character ratios on p0128/p0129 are explained by the rule requiring a rewrite of a one-way indemnity clause; the edits stay confined to the indemnity article and do not touch unrelated text.
The comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, first-person plural and concise, explains the change, cites the playbook position and offers the usual-exclusions plus 3x super-cap fallback.

Minor, non-fatal drafting nits only: the new Licensor paragraph is not lettered '(b)' to match the '(a)' introduced in p0128, and 'API's, Documentation' are referenced without confirmed definitions (mitigated by the catch-all 'any other materials or services provided by Licensor').
